systems.name: Corn leaf-collar staging (Iowa State, Abendroth et al. 2011)
systems.description: VE emergence; V(n) counts leaves with a visible collar (the first leaf has a rounded tip); VT when the last tassel branch is visible; R1 silking, R2 blister, R3 milk, R4 dough, R5 dent, R6 physiological maturity (black layer). Lower leaves are lost from about V6; staging then splits the stalk to find the fifth leaf node. Other methods (droopy-leaf, horizontal-leaf) count one to two leaves more and are not interchangeable.
systems.source: Iowa State University Extension PMR 1009, Corn Growth and Development (Abendroth, Elmore, Boyer, Marlay 2011); Purdue Agronomy, Nielsen, Determining corn leaf stages

systems.name: Soybean staging (Fehr and Caviness 1977)
systems.description: VE, VC, V(n) by fully developed trifoliolate nodes; R1 to R8 from first flower to full maturity.
systems.source: Fehr and Caviness 1977, Stages of soybean development, Iowa State Special Report 80

systems.name: Small-grain staging (Feekes; Zadoks decimal code)
systems.description: Feekes 1 to 11 (emergence to ripening) and the Zadoks 00 to 99 decimal code; tillering, jointing, boot, heading, grain fill.

systems.name: Cotton staging by main-stem node and fruiting
systems.description: Emergence, node counts, first square, first flower, open boll; often expressed as days after planting and nodes above white flower.
systems.source: Extension cotton development guides (Texas A&M, Mississippi State)

systems.name: BBCH decimal code
systems.description: A two-digit code from 00 (dry seed) to 99 (harvested product) with principal stages 0 to 9, defined per crop group; the common international scale.
systems.source: Meier (ed.) 2001, Growth stages of mono- and dicotyledonous plants, BBCH Monograph, Federal Biological Research Centre for Agriculture and Forestry

systems.name: Tree-crop phenology
systems.description: Dormant, bud break, bloom, fruit set, fruit growth, harvest, leaf fall; row geometry does not change with phenology, canopy size changes with age.
systems.source: BBCH monograph (pome and stone fruit, olive, citrus scales)
